name: Worn and soiled (cloth)
describes: Sitting crushes and bends a velvet's pile: pressed patches reflect differently (shading), and abrasion slowly wears the pile down at the front edge and the piping. Hands soil the edges people touch; dust settles on upward faces of cloth. Felt compresses under objects. A stretched wall silk is rarely touched but collects dust at its foot and on any ledge.

abrasion.source: KOTHEA, 'Mohair Velvet Upholstery Fabric, Crib 5 and 100,000 Rubs' (product ranges and specifications), https://www.kothea.com/mohair-velvet-upholstery/
abrasion.conditions: Martindale rubs of a mohair velvet: heavy contract

pileDirection.text: Velvet cut pile up or pile down gives more shine or more saturated colour; pressed pile does the same locally.

mohairResilience.text: Mohair is durable, naturally elastic and crease-resistant.
mohairResilience.source: Wikipedia, 'Mohair', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohair (read 2026-09-26), citing Williams, B. (2007) for the diameter

photograph: Bench tops with lighter and darker patches where the pile lies differently; a worn, shiny front edge on old velvet; grey at the foot of a wall silk.

unverified.reason: The recovery of a mohair pile after sitting was not measured in a source read.
